what_its_for: Propylthiouracil is used to treat an overactive thyroid gland (a condition called hyperthyroidism). It works by slowing down the thyroid gland so it makes less thyroid hormone. It is also sometimes used to prepare patients for thyroid surgery or radioactive iodine treatment.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. Try to take it at evenly spaced times throughout the day (for example, every 8 hours if taking it 3 times a day). Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet. Take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and lab results. The usual starting dose for adults is 300 mg per day, divided into 3 doses (100 mg every 8 hours). Some people with severe hyperthyroidism may need higher doses. Your doctor will likely lower your dose once your thyroid levels become normal. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store propylthiouracil at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking iodine-containing products (such as iodine supplements, certain cough syrups, or large amounts of iodine-rich foods like seaweed) unless your doctor approves them, as iodine can interfere with how this medicine works. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol. Tell your doctor or dentist about this medication before any surgery or dental procedures. Avoid getting sick around others if possible, since this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor RIGHT AWAY or go to the emergency room if you experience: fever, sore throat, mouth sores, or chills (these could be signs of a serious drop in white blood cells called agranulocytosis); yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); unusual bruising or bleeding; skin rash or itching; joint pain or swelling; numbness or tingling; or if you feel very tired or weak. These are serious and potentially life-threatening side effects. Also call your doctor if you notice signs of an underactive thyroid, such as unusual weight gain, feeling cold all the time, or extreme tiredness.
when_it_works: Propylthiouracil does not work immediately. It usually takes several weeks (typically 3 to 6 weeks) before you start to feel better, because it takes time for existing thyroid hormone in your body to be used up. Some people may not feel the full effects for 3 to 6 months. Your doctor will check your thyroid hormone levels with blood tests regularly to monitor how well the medicine is working. Do not stop taking it even if you feel fine, unless your doctor tells you to.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Propylthiouracil is preferred over other thyroid medicines during the first trimester (first 3 months) of pregnancy. However, it carries a risk of serious liver damage to the mother. Your doctor will carefully weigh the risks and benefits. Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Small amounts of this medicine pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. CHILDREN: This medicine is sometimes used in children with hyperthyroidism, but the dose will be carefully adjusted by your doctor based on the child's weight and age. LIVER DISEASE: If you have liver problems, tell your doctor before starting this medicine, as it can cause serious liver damage. Regular liver function monitoring may be needed. ELDERLY: Older adults may need closer monitoring for side effects.
